name: Greece
description: Greece offers expats an appealing Mediterranean lifestyle with a significantly lower cost of living compared to Western Europe and the US. The country boasts a warm climate, rich culture, and an increasingly robust economy, making it an attractive destination for retirees, remote workers, and investors. Recent visa expansions and favorable tax regimes further enhance its appeal.
longdescription: Living in Greece as an expat provides a unique blend of historical charm and modern convenience. The culture is welcoming, with Greeks generally hospitable towards foreigners, and a relaxed pace of life is prevalent. While the economy has faced challenges in the past, it has steadily recovered, driven by tourism, exports, and foreign investment. English is widely spoken, especially in major cities, tourist areas, and among the younger population, easing the transition for newcomers. The country operates a dual-tier healthcare system, offering accessible and often more affordable medical care than in many Western countries. Expat communities are established, particularly in urban centers like Athens and Thessaloniki, as well as on popular islands. Navigating bureaucracy can be a challenge, and the local job market for non-Greek speakers can be limited, but overall, Greece offers a high quality of life with abundant sunshine, fresh local produce, and a rich historical tapestry.

visas.name: Greece Digital Nomad Visa
visas.description: Greece's visa for remote workers who want to live and work from the beautiful Greek islands or mainland.

visas.name: Residence by investment (Greece)
visas.description: Residence by investment program for real estate purchases in Greece, offering EU residency.

visas.name: Greece Student Visa (Type D)
visas.description: Greece's student visa (Type D) for non-EU/EEA nationals enrolled in a full-time study programme at a Greek university or accredited institution for more than 90 days.

visas.name: Greece Family Reunification Permit
visas.description: Greece's family reunification permit allows non-EU spouses and minor dependent children of non-EU residents legally living in Greece for at least two years to join them.

visas.name: Greece Self-Employment Visa
visas.description: Greece's self-employment visa allows non-EU nationals to establish and run their own business or work as an independent professional in Greece, subject to proof of business viability and financial stability.

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Greek citizenship by descent is possible if parents or grandparents are Greek citizens. Individuals must provide documents proving Greek origin to the country's diplomatic mission for migration.

Naturalization.desc: Generally, foreigners can apply for Greek citizenship by naturalization after 7 continuous years of lawful residence in Greece. Applicants must demonstrate sufficient knowledge of the Greek language (typically B1 level), history, and culture, usually through exams. They also need to show integration into Greek society, have a stable income, and a clean criminal record.

Birthright.desc: Information regarding specific 'birthright/soil' rules for citizenship was not explicitly detailed in the search results, though general naturalization pathways require residency. Greek citizenship typically follows the principle of *jus sanguinis* (by descent) rather than *jus soli* (by soil) for automatic citizenship at birth. Children born in Greece to foreign parents can acquire Greek citizenship under certain conditions related to their parents' legal residency and duration, but it is not automatic birthright citizenship in the same way as, for example, in the United States.

Spouse and Family.desc: Marriage to a Greek citizen simplifies the naturalization process. While it does not grant automatic citizenship, it allows individuals to apply for permanent residence in three years and for Greek citizenship in five years, reducing the standard naturalization period. Family members of Golden Visa holders (spouse/registered partner, unmarried children under 21, and parents) can also obtain residence permits and follow the pathway to citizenship through naturalization after meeting the residency requirements.

tax_advice:
*   **Tax Residency:** You become a Greek tax resident if you spend more than 183 days in Greece in a calendar year, or if your center of vital interests is in Greece. Tax residents declare worldwide income; non-residents pay tax only on Greek-source income.
*   **Personal Income Tax:** Progressive rates apply from 9% to 44%. For 2026, the first €10,000 is taxed at 9%, the next €10,000 at 22%, and so on, reaching 44% for income above €40,000. New reforms for 2026 include a 0% tax rate for workers under 25 on their first €20,000 of annual income, and lower rates for families with children.
*   **Corporate Tax:** A flat rate of 22% applies to corporate entities.
*   **VAT (FPA):** The standard VAT rate is 24%, with reduced rates on some islands and essential goods.
*   **Rental Income Tax:** Rental income is taxed separately with progressive rates: 15% on the first €12,000, 25% on €12,001–€35,000, and 45% above €35,000. A 5% automatic deduction covers maintenance.
*   **Dividend Tax:** Dividends are taxed at a low rate of 5%.
*   **Property Tax (ENFIA):** An annual property tax is calculated based on the objective value of real estate holdings.
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** A 15% capital gains tax applies to certain securities and taxable gains. Capital gains tax on transfers of immovable property is suspended through December 31, 2026.
*   **Social Security (EFKA):** Mandatory contributions apply if you are employed in Greece, with a combined standard rate of 35.16% (21.79% for employers and 13.37% for employees), subject to an annual salary cap.
*   **Special Tax Regimes for Expats:**
    *   **Non-Dom Program:** Wealthy individuals can pay a flat €100,000 per year on worldwide income for up to 15 years, provided they have not been Greek tax residents in 7 of the prior 8 years and transfer tax residency to Greece. Family members can be included for an additional €20,000 annually per person.
    *   **Retiree Scheme:** Foreign pensioners may qualify for a flat 7% tax on all qualifying foreign-source income (pensions, dividends, interest) for 15 years.
    *   **Brain Gain Incentive:** New residents working in Greece can receive a 50% income tax exemption on Greek-source employment or business income for up to seven years.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Greece offers a significantly lower cost of living compared to the US and Western Europe, often 30-50% less. A single person can live comfortably for €1,500-€2,300 per month in Athens, including rent, or €800-€1,200 outside the capital. Rent for a one-bedroom apartment in a city center averages around €500-€700, while outside the center it's €200-€450. Groceries for one person typically cost €250-€400 per month.
*   **Language:** While Greek is the official language, English is widely spoken in major cities, tourist areas, and among younger people (35.1% of the population speaks English, rising to 59.7% among those aged 15-34). Learning basic Greek phrases will greatly enhance daily interactions and integration into the local community.
*   **Safety:** Greece is generally very safe, holding a U.S. State Department Level 1 advisory (exercise normal precautions). Violent crime against tourists is rare. Main concerns include petty theft (pickpocketing) in crowded tourist areas and public transport, especially in Athens, and environmental hazards like summer wildfires and extreme heat. Exercise common sense, be aware of your surroundings, and secure belongings.
*   **Registration & Visas:** For stays longer than 90 days, non-EU citizens need a National D visa from a Greek consulate, followed by an in-country application for a residence permit. Popular routes include the Golden Visa for investors (minimum property investment of €250,000, rising to €800,000 in high-demand areas, or other investments), the Digital Nomad Visa (requiring at least €3,500 monthly income), and the Financially Independent Person (FIP) Visa (requiring at least €3,500 monthly passive income). Residence permits are typically issued for 1-5 years and can be renewed. A Greek non-resident tax number and a Greek bank account are necessary for financial transactions.
*   **Healthcare:** Greece has a dual public and private healthcare system. Public healthcare is accessible to registered residents with an AMKA number. Private consultations typically range from €60-€150, and basic health insurance averages around €300 per year. Private health insurance is often required for visa applications.
